title: The human eye & defects
examples: What is accommodation in the eye?
Can the eye focus on things far away?

explain.say: The eye uses a lens to focus light onto the retina.

draw.text: Eye lens focuses light on retina.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the human eye. Look at the cornea, the iris and the pupil. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Accommodation is the eye changing its lens shape. This lets us see near or far.
Myopia means you see distant objects as blurry. Your eye focuses too strongly.
Hypermetropia means close objects look blurry. Your eye focuses too weakly.
To correct myopia, we use a diverging lens. This spreads the light slightly.
Hypermetropia is corrected with a converging lens. This bends light inward correctly.

faq.q: What is the difference between myopic and hyperopic vision?
faq.a: Myopia means your eye focuses light too much, making distant things blurry. Hypermetropia means your eye focuses light too little, making close things blurry.
asks: Why can't I see far away?
What is the problem with focusing distance?

faq.q: Do all eye defects need glasses to fix them?
faq.a: Many defects can be corrected with lenses, but sometimes the eye itself needs other support. Always talk to an eye care professional.

faq.q: How does accommodation actually work in the eye?
faq.a: The ciliary muscles change the shape of the lens. This allows the eye to adjust focus for different distances.
asks: How does the lens change shape?

faq.q: What is a diverging lens used for?
faq.a: A diverging lens spreads out light rays before they enter the eye. This helps correct the focusing issue in myopia.
asks: What is the function of a minus lens?

faq.q: If I read a lot, will my eyes get tired?
faq.a: Yes, focusing for long periods can cause strain. Taking regular breaks and following the twenty-twenty-twenty rule helps greatly.
asks: How can I rest my eyes?

facts: The lens focuses light onto the light-sensitive layer called the retina.
Accommodation is the ability to change focal length.
Myopia is corrected using diverging lenses.
Hypermetropia is corrected using converging lenses.

quiz.say: Which type of lens is used to correct nearsightedness (myopia)?
quiz.why: Diverging lenses spread light slightly to help the eye focus correctly on distant objects.

wrong.0: Convex lenses are converging and are used for hypermetropia.
wrong.2: A converging lens would make the nearsightedness worse by focusing too strongly.
wrong.3: This is a general term; the specific type needed is diverging.

quiz.say: If the eye lens cannot change its shape enough, what process is affected?
quiz.why: Accommodation is the specific term for the eye adjusting its lens shape for focus.

wrong.1: Refraction is the bending of light by the medium, not the changing of the lens itself.
wrong.2: Convergence is the turning of the eyes inwards, which is different from lens focusing.
wrong.3: This is a general concept, but accommodation is the precise biological mechanism.
